evaluatorHazards.title: Nonce / seed grinding
evaluatorHazards.why: 345 of 422 seed-grinding-tagged submissions were promoted. The evaluator hashes the operation stream, so identity tails select a new workload rather than proving a circuit identity.
evaluatorHazards.recommendedAction: Exclude nonce, reroll, and tail grinding from mechanism briefs. Factor them out of causal comparisons.

evaluatorHazards.title: Bundled multi-idea submissions
evaluatorHazards.why: 579 of 949 submissions are mixed-idea routes. Promotion counts on those ideas are not component effects.
evaluatorHazards.recommendedAction: Use one-change ablations or factorials for mechanism claims. Keep mixed submissions as search history only.

literatureOverlay.claim: The strongest publicly auditable discovery systems search an executable representation against a hard external evaluator, not an undifferentiated knowledge graph.
literatureOverlay.implication: Compile disposable decision briefs from immutable Atlas records. Do not add graph infrastructure until an equal-content representation factorial earns an effect.
literatureOverlay.boundary: This describes where evidence is easiest to audit, not a controlled proof that executable domains produce the most important innovations.

literatureOverlay.claim: Knowledge presentation and advice are not a sufficient mechanism for strategy revision. In PostTrainBench, only 2.08% of adjacent recognized experiment pairs changed objective family, data-source type, or stage structure.

sources.citation: What Is Missing from AI Post-Training AI, arXiv:2608.19072

literatureOverlay.implication: A compiled ECDSA brief can prevent rediscovery and stale claims. It should not be assumed to reallocate search.
literatureOverlay.boundary: Observational corpus; 44 trajectories did probe alternatives. Not a causal result on Yukon agents.

literatureOverlay.claim: Cross-session memory can accelerate rediscovery while high memory injection reduces strategy diversity; a cold condition can still find the best point.
literatureOverlay.implication: Hard-filter evaluator hazards and duplicated lineage. Do not broadcast the full submission archive into every prompt.
literatureOverlay.boundary: Three sessions per configuration on one kernel task; reported token reduction is not total cost to a verified frontier.

literatureOverlay.claim: On autoresearch, classical TPE and CMA-ES beat pure LLM search; the best reported system kept a classical optimizer on the trajectory and let an LLM inject occasional domain-informed proposals.
literatureOverlay.implication: Prefer schedule/width/ladder search with a classical controller. Reserve LLM budget for representation proposals and diagnosis.
literatureOverlay.boundary: Result is task-specific. It does not license deleting Atlas provenance.

literatureOverlay.claim: The 2026 open circuit that matches Google's unpublished secp256k1 Pareto points is Schrottenloher's EEA-dialog / ping-pong inversion, with jump-GCD and Gidney venting as the main published knobs.

sources.citation: Schrottenloher, Optimized Point Addition Circuits, arXiv:2606.02235

literatureOverlay.implication: Treat ping-pong / dialog inversion as a representation-class change. Local Kaliski-era tuning does not transfer automatically across this cut.
literatureOverlay.boundary: Published counts use a different contract than the pinned ECDSA.fail 9,024-shot verified scorer. Do not subtract those Toffoli numbers from Atlas scores.

literatureOverlay.claim: Babbush et al. reported low-qubit and low-gate secp256k1 point-add operating points but did not publish the circuits, relying on a zero-knowledge proof. The ECDSA.fail README quotes 1,175 qubits / 2.7M Toffoli and 1,425 qubits / 2.1M Toffoli.

sources.citation: Schrottenloher discussion of Babbush et al., arXiv:2606.02235

literatureOverlay.implication: Use those numbers only as an external aspirational target, never as an Atlas floor or as evidence that a named mechanism is present in the sealed corpus.
literatureOverlay.boundary: Kickmick / approximate-success circuits are not the ECDSA.fail exact classical+phase+ancilla contract.

literatureOverlay.claim: Gidney measurement-based uncomputation and temporary AND remain the standard Toffoli-saving uncompute pattern; Atlas has a jointly qualified one-change ablation of the temporary-AND family.

sources.citation: Gidney, Halving the cost of quantum addition, Quantum 2, 74 (2018)

literatureOverlay.implication: Keep measurement-uncomputation as a live algorithm family. Isolated Atlas effect is recorded separately as artifact_verified.
literatureOverlay.boundary: The paper does not by itself identify the ECDSA.fail delta. Causal score movement requires the Atlas ablation.

literatureOverlay.claim: A public note declared the product-square closed after pricing one algorithm, then a later recursion level (Karatsuba-2) invalidated that closure.

sources.citation: Yukon KG NOTE.md research cutoff 2026-08-23, section 11.2

literatureOverlay.implication: Store closures as scoped assertions with reopen conditions. Never merge a retracted ceiling into current-best prose.
literatureOverlay.boundary: The sealed Atlas snapshot records Karatsuba as historical observation, not a jointly qualified one-change ablation.

literatureOverlay.claim: The trusted evaluator derives inputs from SHAKE256 of the semantic operation stream, so identity padding and nonce grinding select a new Fiat-Shamir sample rather than proving an algorithmic mechanism.
literatureOverlay.implication: Classify seed grinding as an evaluator hazard. Do not promote it as a supported mechanism even when it dominates promotion counts.
literatureOverlay.boundary: Competition realism may still use nonce search. Primary mechanism claims must freeze or factor it out.

caveats: Official one-change deltas are scoped to their parent artifacts. They are not additive with each other or with the current frontier score.
Frontier submissions in this snapshot still bundle nonce grinding with structural edits, so the champion score is not a pure mechanism effect.
Atlas reports baseline 10704574395 and frontier 1182644586 qubit-Toffoli product, with no compatible nontrivial product floor.
The 512-qubit floor is a pinned two-register interface bound, not a universal ECC lower bound. Current frontier width is 1150.
Published Google/Schrottenloher Pareto points use a different contract than the pinned ECDSA.fail scorer.
This brief is a disposable presentation-plane compilation. It does not mutate Atlas releases and has not earned an innovation-accelerator claim.
